answer: A saffron market beside a dune could set a short earning horizon: each key must solve a fresh memory-hard puzzle for that epoch. Its input combines the public key with an unpredictable beacon; validators check the proof and reject another key's solution or an old epoch. Every added alias needs another computation, memory allocation and electricity, even when a farm runs them in parallel. Difficulty must cost more than the alias's extra reward. This assumes no cheap puzzle shortcut and a credible reward cap; newcomers need an affordable small-device difficulty.
